walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 2: Language Diversity and Change — a core area of A-Level English Language.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: Language Diversity and Change brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 2: Language Diversity and Change.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Who wrote first major English dictionary?
options: Johnson
Webster
Murray
Skeat

mcqs.q: Is language change a sign of decline?
options: Language change shows that standards are falling and English is being ruined.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
Language change only happens in informal speech, not in writing.
No — modern linguistics treats change as natural and continuous, not as decay. Every language has always been changing and will continue to.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
Language change only happens in informal speech, not in writing.
Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.

mcqs.q: What is Skinner's behaviourist view of language acquisition?
options: Children learn language through imitation and operant conditioning — they are reinforced for correct utterances and corrected for errors.
Language change only happens in informal speech, not in writing.
Skinner believed in an innate grammar module.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
